plan: My private value is $27. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is often to bid close to my true value. Since the prize is won by the highest bidder but paid at the third-highest price, I want to bid strategically. I'll bid slightly above my value to increase my chances of winning, but not so high that I risk negative profit. A bid around $30-$32 seems reasonable to balance winning probability and potential profit margin.

My private value is $31. To maximize profit, I want to win only if I can do so without paying more than my value. Since bids are independent and values are randomly drawn, I'll aim to bid strategically near my value. A bid slightly below my value (around $28-$30) gives me a good chance of winning while preserving potential profit margin. This allows some buffer against other bidders while still reflecting my true valuation.

My private value is $20. The optimal strategy is to bid close to, but not exceeding, my true value. Since the winning bid pays the third-highest bid, I want to bid strategically. A bid slightly above my value (around $22-$25) gives me a chance to win while minimizing potential overpayment. Other bidders likely have values between $0-$49, so a moderate bid that's not too aggressive or too conservative seems prudent.
